offending_extra_words: (except that no settlement imposing liability, admission of fault, or a non-monetary obligation on the indemnified party may be made without its prior written consent)
The indemnified party may participate with counsel of its own choosing at its own cost.
A delay in notice relieves the indemnifying party only to the extent it is materially prejudiced.

20.5 If the Services or Deliverables are, or in Vendor's reasonable opinion are likely to become, the subject of an infringement claim, Vendor shall at its expense and Customer's option procure the right for Customer to continue using them, or modify or replace them with functionally equivalent, non-infringing items that continue to meet the agreed specifications and service levels.
together with Fees paid for Services and Deliverables Customer can no longer reasonably use
reasons: Every atomic element of the preferred position is expressly present: Vendor defence and indemnity for Customer and Affiliates, IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct, notice/control/cooperation procedure, and a Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

The fallback is incomplete because no 3x annual fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity obligations was inserted; the locked target is preferred, so this does not defeat the redline but the levels cannot be mixed.

Minimality fails: the insertion goes beyond the preferred prose by adding hold-harmless language, an express Customer duty to defend, detailed settlement-consent and participation mechanics, a materially-prejudiced notice qualifier, and the fallback-level infringement remedies in 20.5 (including refund of fees for unusable Deliverables).

Intent is preserved: the clause fills a genuine gap that Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 already assume, uses only defined terms (Affiliates, Applicable Law, Customer Data, Deliverables, Vendor Technology, Order Form, Fees), and leaves 19.5 and 21.3 fully effective, with 9.3's cross-reference to Section 20.5 now resolving.

Anchoring nit: the new Section 20 heading and its subsections were all inserted after the same paragraph (19.5); they should be sequenced so the heading precedes its body without relying on reverse-order insertion.
